sections.content:
146,420 people

were counted on the census as "IT managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
IT managers co-ordinate the provision of IT services and functions in an organisation.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "IT managers", 17.3% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "IT managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "IT managers" included:

  • human resource managers and directors
  • IT project managers
  • marketing, sales and advertising directors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "IT managers" there were more men than women (75.3% compared with 24.7%).

This means "IT managers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 75.3% and women made up 24.7% of "IT managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "IT managers" included:

  • industrial cleaning process occupations
  • building and civil engineering technicians
  • production, factory and assembly supervisors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "IT managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "IT managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "IT managers", 7.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (94.6% compared with 5.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (97%) than self-employed (3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
